newsitem.title: UK: C&W says in talks with Veba on alliance.
newsitem.headline: C&W says in talks with Veba on alliance.

text.p: Britain's Cable and Wireless Plc said on Tuesday it was in talks with German utility Veba AG about the future of their partnership, amid press speculation that the British firm may pull out of the alliance.

"Cable and Wireless and Veba are in discussion about the future of their partnerships in Germany and the rest of Europe," the company said in a statement. "The discussions are continuing and a more detailed statement will be made in due course."
C&W and Veba formed a strategic alliance, called Vebacom, in 1995. Last year, the firms agreed to bring RWE into the alliance and final contracts were drawn up two weeks ago.

But C&W has not yet signed the deal, and British newpspapers have speculated it is poised to pull out of the German partnership to join a larger global alliance like the Global One partnership of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp of the U.S.

Meanwhile, German sources said Veba had already offered C&W terms to leave the partnership. Under the terms, Veba would give C&W its stake in C&W Europe and buy back C&W's 45-percent stake in their joint venture Vebacom.
Veba would keep its 10.4 percent stake in C&W under the terms of the offer, the source said. A spokeswoman for Veba said she could not confirm or deny the offer had been made.
